item.title: His Highness the Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani begins official talks in Berlin today, where he is due to meet German President Frank…
item.description:
His Highness the Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani begins official talks in Berlin today, where he is due to meet German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Federal Chancellor Friedrich Merz, having arrived from Bern on Thursday evening to a 21-gun salute. The visit aims to advance the strategic partnership in trade, investment, energy and security. The two countries have had diplomatic relations since 1973 and in May 2023 signed a memorandum establishing a strategic dialogue. The Amir was seen off at Bern Airport by Swiss President Guy Parmelin, to whom he sent a cable of thanks.
Sources: Gulf Times (QNA) https://www.gulf-times.com/article/738621/qatar/hh-the-amir-in-berlin-to-bolster-ties-with-germany · The Peninsula https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/19/11/2026/amir-arrives-in-germany-1 · Qatar Tribune (QNA) https://www.qatar-tribune.com/article/265452/latest-news/amir-departs-switzerland-for-germany

item.title: HE Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Minister of Interior and Commander of the Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya), concluded h…
item.description:
HE Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, Minister of Interior and Commander of the Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya), concluded his visit to Pakistan by meeting Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, after signing with Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, in the presence of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, a security cooperation MoU between Lekhwiya and Pakistan's Federal Constabulary and an action plan against drug smuggling. The two sides agreed to expand the Police Officers Exchange Programme, strengthen cooperation between Qatar's National Cyber Security Agency and Pakistan's cybercrime agency, and deepen counterterrorism coordination.

item.title: The Ministry of Interior continues to explain Traffic Law No. 19 of 2026, effective 19 December: light electric vehicles such as scooters m…
item.description:
The Ministry of Interior continues to explain Traffic Law No. 19 of 2026, effective 19 December: light electric vehicles such as scooters must be registered with the licensing authority and fees paid before road use, and carrying passengers on motorcycles, bicycles and scooters is prohibited. Article 75 limits horn use to imminent danger and bans air and musical horns, with a QR500 settlement, rising to QR1,000 for fitting sound and light devices reserved for emergency vehicles without written permission. Article 76 bans dazzling lights except when weather requires them, with a QR500 settlement. The law gives a six-month grace period to owners of vehicles registered under the 2007 law.
Sources: The Peninsula https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/19/11/2026/new-traffic-law-introduces-regulations-for-electric-scooters · The Peninsula https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/19/11/2026/moi-clarifies-proper-use-of-horn-dazzling-lights-under-new-traffic-law · Qatar Tribune https://www.qatar-tribune.com/article/265030/latest-news/new-traffic-law-enhances-road-safety-keeps-pace-with-advances-in-transportation-interior-ministry

item.title: Qatar strongly condemned Israeli occupation incursions into rural Quneitra and Daraa in southern Syria and repeated attacks on civilians, i…
item.description:
Qatar strongly condemned Israeli occupation incursions into rural Quneitra and Daraa in southern Syria and repeated attacks on civilians, including women, children and older people, calling them a flagrant breach of Syria's sovereignty and a grave threat to regional security. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs urged the international community to compel Israel to comply with international resolutions, particularly the 1974 disengagement agreement, and reiterated Qatar's full support for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

item.title: The organising committee announced details of the second Doha International Music and Marching Festival (Doha Tattoo), from 14 to 17 Decemb…
item.description:
The organising committee announced details of the second Doha International Music and Marching Festival (Doha Tattoo), from 14 to 17 December 2026 at Katara Cultural Village under the patronage of the Minister of Interior, with nine bands representing eight countries alongside Qatari bands, more than 1,000 participants and the Qatar Philharmonic Orchestra. The United Kingdom, Oman and Kazakhstan return for a second year, while France, Pakistan, Armenia, Uzbekistan and Egypt take part for the first time. Last year's first edition brought together bands from seven countries.

item.title: Saudi Civil Defense announced on Thursday evening that a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was targeted in a Houthi attack…
item.description:
Saudi Civil Defense announced on Thursday evening that a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was targeted in a Houthi attack, causing material damage to several floors and neighbouring buildings with no casualties. Reports said the damaged tower is the headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, the capital's tallest building at 80 storeys and 385 metres, with the fund managing more than $900 billion in assets; it was the second attack on the financial district this month. An official spokesman called the targeting of civilian infrastructure a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law.

item.description:
Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman met US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Riyadh to discuss defence cooperation, while US President Donald Trump said he wants a "lasting" deal with Iran and will end the conflict "one way or the other", adding there is an "indication" Tehran is pursuing biological weapons. item.title: Air defences in Kuwait and Bahrain repelled Iranian aerial attacks; Iran's army said its drones targeted Patriot systems and launch platfor…
item.description:
Air defences in Kuwait and Bahrain repelled Iranian aerial attacks; Iran's army said its drones targeted Patriot systems and launch platforms at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, while neither Kuwait nor Bahrain reported damage or casualties. Kuwait's Foreign Ministry called the attack a "flagrant violation of its sovereignty", and GCC Secretary-General Jassim Al-Budaiwi held Iran responsible for the escalation. The coalition said it destroyed 60 Houthi targets in Sanaa, Amran, Saada and Hodeidah.

item.title: Airlines extended suspensions to Saudi Arabia as tensions rose: Etihad cancelled passenger and cargo flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh a…
item.description:

item.title: Oman celebrates its 56th National Day today, Friday 20 November, and Sultan Haitham bin Tarik pardoned 344 prisoners for the occasion. Oman…
item.description:
Oman celebrates its 56th National Day today, Friday 20 November, and Sultan Haitham bin Tarik pardoned 344 prisoners for the occasion. Oman Vision 2040 figures show public debt falling from 65.9% to 34.6% of GDP, public revenues up 16% to about RO9.828 billion by the end of Q3 2026, and GDP at constant prices growing 5.1% in Q2, with S&P raising its 2026 growth forecast to about 3.5%. The National Day holiday runs from 25 to 28 November.
Sources: Gulf News (ONA) https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/oman/sultan-haitham-pardons-344-prisoners-ahead-of-omans-56th-national-day-1.500753148 · Times of Oman https://timesofoman.com/article/179307-oman-set-to-celebrate-national-day-with-renewed-economic-momentum · Oman Observer (ONA) https://www.omanobserver.om/article/1199868/oman/oman-to-mark-national-day-on-friday-nov-20 · Saudi Press Agency https://www.spa.gov.sa/en/N2731248

item.description:

item.description:
President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Libyan Government of National Unity head Abdulhamid Dbeibah witnessed in Cairo the signing of nine agreements and memoranda, in the presence of Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, including a framework agreement on natural gas infrastructure, another on refining petroleum products and an MoU on energy and natural resources, alongside fisheries, media, higher education, labour, small enterprises and training. item.description:
Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said Egypt is constantly working to de-escalate in the region, coordinating with the GCC, Pakistan, Turkey and the United States, and maintaining contacts with Iran. He said the target of 600 aid trucks a day into Gaza has not been met, and phase-two talks on Israeli withdrawal, early recovery and reconstruction have not yet begun.
